object_description: aggregated gymnasium and workroom volume forming the upper end of the complex along a hollow alley
design_condition: the aggregated volume forms the upper end of the school complex, with a staircase and an alley cut through it as an extension of the pedestrian access axis opening the school rooms and playing field above

positive: The aggregation of gymnasium and workrooms forms the upper end of the school complex
A spatial break is created as a staircase and alley extending the pedestrian access axis
This opens up the school rooms and the playing field on the upper level
The building is clearly part of the school complex
It has relatively little impact on the spatial design of the town entrance
The necessary outdoor spaces are of attractive quality
Hall and workrooms share a common access area and the school rooms are also reached via the large staircase
The workrooms are reached via an attractively proportioned vestibule-like access area
They are well arranged and well lit
The building appears and is of high quality construction and materialisation
Differentiated materialisations, glazing and spatial formulations show a high level of architectural competence
negative: The building occupies a large area of the perimeter
The outdoor spaces are overall arranged too small and too angled
The double access disposition seems unclear as to whether staircase or hall is primary
The visitor must leave the main route and enter the building laterally through a layer of serving rooms
The gallery cannot take up the full width of the halls due to lack of space
Since the alley is not strictly hollow the privacy of the school rooms suffers
The complex building shell tends to lead to above-average costs despite the compact volume
The project does not succeed in implementing the promises made
The double access leads to an unclear situation and the elaborate alley leads nowhere
The building structure remains self-referential and the effort required is too great
